stories.t: Gunfire at a Fairfield Halloween store leaves one dead and six hurt
stories.s: Police say a gunman opened fire inside a Spirit Halloween store at Solano Town Center on Friday around 8:30 p.m., killing one person and wounding six. At least three of the injured were in critical condition, and no arrest had been reported. Detectives are interviewing witnesses and asking anyone with information to call Fairfield police.
stories.w: Fairfield is about an hour’s drive from the Peninsula, and the shooting happened during a holiday weekend when stores and events draw crowds across the Bay Area.

stories.t: Analysis: 42% of names on DOJ’s “likely noncitizen” list aren’t on California’s voter rolls
stories.s: Two UCLA data scientists reviewed the list the Trump administration sent California in early October and found that 8,880 of its roughly 21,000 names do not appear in the state’s current voter files. The analysis was filed in court Saturday by an immigrant-rights group and a candidate for governor, who argue that many eligible citizens were wrongly flagged. A federal appeals court ruled against the administration’s complaint a second time on Friday.
stories.w: With Election Day on Tuesday, the fight over this list affects whether flagged voters in San Mateo County and across California have their ballots counted.

stories.t: Daylight saving time ends: set clocks back an hour
stories.s: Clocks “fall back” this weekend as daylight saving time ends, giving most people an extra hour of sleep. A sleep specialist interviewed by CBS News offers tips for easing the adjustment, which can leave some people groggy for a few days.
stories.w: Phones update on their own, but stove, car and wall clocks do not, and darker evenings arrive just as commutes on Caltrain and BART shift back toward dusk.

stories.t: Valkyries win the WNBA title in Game 7 for the franchise’s first championship
stories.s: The Golden State Valkyries beat the Atlanta Dream 68–63 on Saturday in San Francisco, winning the title in just their second season. Gabby Williams scored 30 points, 28 of them in the second half, and was named Finals MVP. A championship parade runs along the Embarcadero on Wednesday, Nov. 4, with fans able to line up from 9 a.m.

stories.t: Today in sports: Warriors rest Curry, 49ers regroup on a bye, Quakes are playoff-bound
stories.s: The Warriors beat the Lakers 112–95 on Friday, with Stephen Curry scoring 31, and play the Clippers on Sunday without him: the team says he is sitting out for injury management because of a lingering knee issue. The 49ers are on a bye after last week’s 29–20 loss in Atlanta. The San Jose Earthquakes have already clinched a spot in the MLS playoffs, which begin Nov. 18, and were fourth in the West when they clinched.

stories.t: 49ers add DeForest Buckner, but a trade for Jauan Jennings fell through
stories.s: San Francisco recently acquired two-time All-Pro defensive tackle DeForest Buckner from the Colts for a 2027 fourth-round pick. Newsweek, citing a Fox Sports report, says the team also worked out terms for Vikings receiver Jauan Jennings, but he declined to say he wanted to return and the deal died. Coach Kyle Shanahan has said receivers Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and Demarcus Robinson could be back after the bye.

stories.t: NFL fines 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw $12,537 for a punch at a Falcons receiver
stories.s: The league fined Greenlaw for a punch aimed at the ball that instead landed on Atlanta receiver Drake London’s head in the Week 7 loss. Reports say it is his second fine of the season.

stories.t: Netflix renews “The Diplomat” for a fifth season
stories.s: Netflix confirmed Thursday that the political thriller starring Keri Russell and Rufus Sewell will return, two weeks after season four debuted on Oct. 15. The show has spent 13 weeks in Netflix’s global Top 10. No release date or story details have been announced yet.

stories.t: Next up on streaming: “Black Doves,” “Rings of Power” and “12 12 12”
stories.s: November’s early premieres include season two of the British spy series “Black Doves” on Netflix on Nov. 5 and season three of “The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power” on Prime Video on Nov. 11, with four episodes at once and weekly releases after. Apple TV+ launches the crime-thriller miniseries “12 12 12” on Nov. 13.

stories.t: NASA asks industry how to lift Hubble into a safer orbit
stories.s: NASA issued a request for information asking companies how they could raise, service or safely bring down the Hubble Space Telescope, aiming for a mission by 2032 that would lift it to at least 600 kilometers. Without help, Hubble is expected to fall back to Earth in the early-to-mid 2030s. NASA says it is only gathering ideas and has not committed to paying for a rescue.

stories.t: Mistral publishes the weights of its trillion-parameter Large 4 model
stories.s: The French AI company released the downloadable weights for Mistral Large 4, so companies and governments can run it on their own systems. It is pitched at cybersecurity work and coding agents, and Mistral says it matches a leading Chinese open model while using 47 percent fewer tokens per task. The weights are on Hugging Face and the model is also available through Mistral’s API.

stories.t: Four-person crew finishes a 378-day simulated Mars mission
stories.s: NASA’s second CHAPEA crew stepped out of a 3D-printed habitat at Johnson Space Center on Saturday after more than a year of isolation. The four volunteers grew crops in simulated Martian soil and worked with limited resources and communication delays, so researchers can learn how astronauts stay healthy on long trips.

stories.t: Data centers and AI become a midterm issue, even in Brooklyn
stories.s: At a political event five days before Election Day, conversation kept returning to AI and data centers, according to TechCrunch. A recent industry report found nearly $200 billion of data center projects were delayed or blocked in the first half of 2026 amid local opposition.

stories.t: Layoffs pile up as October ends, including cuts in San Francisco
stories.s: Companies announcing cuts this week included Comcast, Amazon’s devices unit, Disney’s theme parks, and Alaska Air Group, which plans about 200 non-contract job cuts including 48 in Hawaii. In San Francisco, state notices list 57 jobs at Dropbox and 53 at Front, and a Levy operation in Oakland will close Dec. 31 with 181 workers affected.
stories.w: Bay Area tech cuts are small but steady, a sign of a tougher local job market heading into the holidays.

stories.t: Tech money makes up at least a fifth of outside spending in California legislative races
stories.s: Spending on Assembly and Senate races topped $128 million as of Oct. 29, up from $74 million in 2022, and groups funded by Google, Meta, and other tech interests account for at least 20% of contributions to outside spenders. Unlike candidate donations, which are capped at $5,900, these independent expenditures have no limit.
stories.w: Outside money is shaping the people who will write California’s rules on AI, data centers, and tech jobs that matter to Peninsula workers.

stories.t: Warriors beat the Lakers 112–95 to reach .500
stories.s: Warriors: beat the Lakers 112–95 on Friday at Chase Center in an NBA Cup game for their third straight win, evening their record at 3–3; they host the Clippers on Sunday. 49ers: 6–1, back from their bye next week. Giants: off-season. Earthquakes: waiting on the MLS Cup Playoffs.

stories.t: Halloween night sky: Saturn and early fireballs
stories.s: Around 7 p.m., look east-southeast for Saturn, a bright yellow-white point about two fists above the horizon; a small telescope shows its nearly edge-on rings. Early Taurid meteors, the so-called Halloween fireballs, can streak from the east-northeast, with the shower peaking in the second week of November.

stories.t: China’s secretive space plane is visible before dawn this week
stories.s: Shenlong, China’s reusable space plane on its fourth mission, can be seen as a steady moving point of light in the predawn sky. In California, a good pass is expected over Los Angeles early on Nov. 2; Bay Area skywatchers can find local times on Heavens-Above.

stories.t: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Rosalind for life sciences research
stories.s: OpenAI released GPT-6 Rosalind, a model built for biological reasoning and scientific tool use. Access is limited to approved organizations through the company’s trusted-access program for research.

stories.t: Halloween weekend brings a coastal flood advisory and a chance of drizzle
stories.s: A coastal flood advisory covers shoreline areas of San Francisco and San Pablo bays through 6 p.m. Sunday, with up to 1.9 feet of water possible in low spots. Rain spreads into the Bay Area later Saturday, so trick-or-treaters may see light drizzle, with highs in the low 60s.
stories.w: Plan Halloween routes away from flood-prone bayside streets near high tide, and bring a light rain layer for kids.

stories.t: Could Prop. 45 open the door to more California data centers?
stories.s: Prop. 45 is pitched as a pro-housing overhaul of environmental review, but legal scholars say its streamlining for telecom and support infrastructure could let data centers sidestep a new state law. Supporters, who have raised more than $40 million including $3 million from PG&E, say data centers aren’t covered, and at least 26 cities and counties have moved to limit them.
stories.w: Data centers draw heavily on the power grid and water, which affects utility bills and local planning on the Peninsula.

stories.t: Today in sports: Warriors host the Lakers in an NBA Cup game
stories.s: Warriors: 2–3 after Wednesday’s 119–114 win at Minnesota; they host the Lakers tonight at Chase Center in an NBA Cup game. 49ers: bye week at 6–1. Giants: trimming the roster ahead of the off-season. Earthquakes: waiting on the MLS Cup Playoffs.

stories.t: New this weekend: Apple TV’s Nocturne and Dexter: Resurrection season 2
stories.s: Apple TV premieres Nocturne with two episodes, starring Liev Schreiber as a soldier turned homicide detective and Stephen Graham as a serial killer, and also airs the Dark Matter season 2 finale. Paramount+ launches the second season of Dexter: Resurrection, and the Daytime Emmys stream tonight.

stories.t: New music Friday: THAO, Sampa the Great, DIIV, and Queens of the Stone Age
stories.s: THAO’s Show Me is a personal record about divorce and change, and Sampa the Great’s Nu Zamrock blends Zambia’s 1970s Zamrock sound with hip-hop and soul. DIIV teams with producer A.G. Cook on the glossier ZIRP!, and Queens of the Stone Age also have a new album out.

stories.t: Astronauts mark the 100th US spacewalk from the space station
stories.s: NASA’s Anil Menon and Canada’s Joshua Kutryk spent 7 hours and 11 minutes outside the station installing an upgraded solar array that unrolled to 63 feet on its own. It was the first spacewalk by a Canadian since 2019, and the pair go out again Nov. 5 to add the last new array.

stories.t: Virgin Galactic’s new space plane flies for the first time
stories.s: Apeiron, the first of Virgin Galactic’s Delta-class ships, flew beneath its carrier plane from Arizona to Spaceport America in New Mexico for testing. The company plans to start carrying paying customers in spring 2027, with nearly 700 ticket holders waiting.

stories.t: ChatGPT Pro and Business subscribers can claim up to $500 a month in API credits
stories.s: OpenAI says eligible ChatGPT Pro and Business subscribers can now claim up to $500 a month in free API credits by linking an API organization they own, making it cheaper to try building with OpenAI’s models.

stories.t: Fed holds rates at 3.75% to 4% as two officials push for a hike
stories.s: The Federal Reserve kept its benchmark rate unchanged after September’s increase, with Beth Hammack and Lisa Cook dissenting in favor of another quarter-point hike. The statement gave no clear signal about December, as inflation ran at 3.7% in September and energy prices stay high.
stories.w: Steady but high rates keep mortgages, car loans, and credit cards expensive in one of the country’s priciest housing markets.

stories.t: Judge refuses to make California set aside 20,000 ballots
stories.s: US District Judge David O. Carter rejected the Trump administration’s request to set aside ballots from voters it says might not be citizens, citing a pattern of attempted election interference. Prosecutors conceded some people on the federal list are likely citizens, and the administration plans to appeal.
stories.w: San Mateo County ballots are counted under the same state rules, so the ruling keeps local counting on its normal track.

stories.t: High-speed rail chief resigns amid a travel spending scandal
stories.s: Ian Choudri stepped down as CEO of the California High-Speed Rail Authority, effective immediately, after reports that nearly $600,000 went to questionable consultant trips. State Finance Director Joe Stephenshaw takes over a project now estimated at $126 billion to $231 billion.
stories.w: The Peninsula is part of the planned San Francisco-to-Los Angeles route, sharing Caltrain’s corridor.

stories.t: Measure V asks San Mateo County voters to extend an $848 million college bond
stories.s: The bond would fund a new gym, arts building upgrades, and repairs at Cañada College, College of San Mateo, and Skyline College, extending an existing tax of $18 per $100,000 of assessed value through 2049. Critics point to a past bribery scandal tied to earlier bond contracts, which led to a former chancellor’s jail sentence.
stories.w: A median-priced county home would pay about $386 a year, and Skyline and CSM are the closest campuses to Millbrae.

stories.t: Curry scores 44 as the Warriors win at Minnesota
stories.s: Warriors: beat the Timberwolves 119–114 on Wednesday behind 44 points from Stephen Curry; Jonathan Kuminga led Minnesota with 20. Golden State is 2–3 and hosts the Lakers on Friday. 49ers: bye week at 6–1. Earthquakes: waiting on the MLS Cup Playoffs.

stories.t: Giants start a pivotal off-season with pitching at the top of the list
stories.s: San Francisco finished with 24 players on the injured list and must trim to 40-man roster limits within days. The front office wants at least two starters behind Logan Webb and Landen Roupp plus a closer, and may try to trade a big contract, all before a possible lockout on Dec. 1.

stories.t: Patrick Stewart, Star Trek’s Captain Picard, dies at 86
stories.s: Stewart died Wednesday at his home in Los Angeles after a short struggle with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia, his spokesperson said. He played Jean-Luc Picard across seven seasons, four films, and Star Trek: Picard, and Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men films, alongside a celebrated Shakespearean stage career.

stories.t: Google unveils Gemini 4 Carbon, starting with cybersecurity defenders
stories.s: Google calls Gemini 4 Carbon its strongest model for long, multi-step engineering work and cybersecurity tasks such as finding and patching vulnerabilities. Access starts with a group of cyber defenders, and Google says developers, businesses, and consumers will get it after more feedback and safety work.

stories.t: SpaceX test-fires Starship ahead of Flight 15
stories.s: SpaceX completed static fires of Ship 42, including a full-duration burn of all six engines, after testing the Super Heavy booster that will fly with it. Elon Musk is targeting November for Flight 15 and wants to try catching both the ship and the booster, pending approval.

stories.t: About $164 million has flowed through Mayor Lurie’s political and charity network
stories.s: The San Francisco Standard tallied roughly $124 million in private donations to city efforts and $39 million in political money tied to Lurie since 2023, plus $10 million of his own in 2024. Four November measures he backs, including three charter reforms and a Muni parcel tax, have raised $18.6 million.
stories.w: Many Peninsula commuters rely on Muni and BART connections in the city, so the San Francisco measures on this ballot shape regional transit too.

stories.t: Most California Republicans in Congress skip a pledge to seat election winners
stories.s: A bipartisan pledge to oppose efforts to undermine free and fair elections has 17 signers, including five California Democrats. Rep. Kevin Kiley, now an independent, was the only member of California’s Republican delegation to sign; several others did not respond. The pledge aims to head off a repeat of the pressure on Congress after the 2020 election.
stories.w: With the House majority razor-thin, how California’s representatives handle certification could matter for the whole country.

stories.t: Today in sports: Warriors visit Minnesota tonight
stories.s: Warriors: 1–3 after Monday’s 134–114 win at Denver; they play at Minnesota tonight. 49ers: bye week at 6–1. Giants: off-season. Earthquakes: waiting on the MLS Cup Playoffs.

stories.t: Final Dune: Part Three trailer lands ahead of a Dec. 18 release
stories.s: The last trailer for Denis Villeneuve’s Dune: Part Three, starring Timothée Chalamet and Zendaya, leans into war on Arrakis and Paul’s turn toward tyranny, with a bigger role for Chani than in the novel. The film opens in theaters only on Dec. 18, the same holiday stretch as Avengers: Doomsday.

stories.t: Astronomers spot a possible new dwarf planet beyond Neptune
stories.s: Data from the Vera C. Rubin Observatory revealed 2026 ED138, an object estimated at 600 to 1,500 kilometers across about 46 times farther from the sun than Earth. If its size is confirmed, likely with infrared telescopes such as JWST, it would become the sixth known dwarf planet.

stories.t: GitHub Copilot Fusion picks the AI model for each request
stories.s: Instead of choosing a model yourself, Copilot Fusion routes each prompt, sometimes drafting with a lighter model and escalating or having a second model review the work. It is available on all Copilot plans in VS Code, the GitHub CLI, and JetBrains tools, with a temporary 30% discount for paid users.

stories.t: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees
stories.s: Microsoft offered a voluntary exit package to roughly a quarter of its workforce at level 70 and below in the US, Canada, India, and the UK, with each business unit deciding whether to take part. Those who accept leave by year-end with standard severance, and the company said layoffs remain possible.
stories.w: Microsoft is a major Bay Area employer, and big-tech buyouts ripple through local hiring and the housing market.

stories.t: King tides flood bayside roads, with more high water due this week
stories.s: High tides swamped parts of Marin on Monday, flooding a Highway 101 off-ramp and stranding drivers and pedestrians until the water receded. A coastal flood advisory for low-lying shoreline areas runs through Thursday afternoon, with San Francisco’s highest tides about 2 feet above normal around midday today.
stories.w: Bayfront areas along the Peninsula, including near Millbrae and Burlingame, can see the same midday flooding, so avoid shoreline paths and low roads around high tide.

stories.t: California’s last-minute voting guide: mail ballots must be postmarked by Nov. 3
stories.s: Mail ballots count if they are postmarked by Election Day and arrive within seven days, and early voting centers are open in every county. The ballot carries 14 statewide propositions, including Prop. 40, which would make California the first state with a billionaire tax, plus races for governor and several competitive House seats.
stories.w: Peninsula voters can still mail a ballot, drop it off, or vote in person at any San Mateo County vote center through Election Day.

stories.t: A river otter returns to the San Mateo coast after more than 100 years
stories.s: Wildlife cameras in a closed area of the Cloverdale Ranch preserve near Pescadero caught a North American river otter this summer, the first documented on the San Mateo coast since the 1800s. Biologists say the otter, which needs clean water and plenty of food, is a sign the creeks there are healthy.
stories.w: It’s a hopeful sign for the county’s coastal creeks, which also support coho salmon and steelhead.

stories.t: Warriors earn their first win, routing Denver 134–114
stories.s: Warriors: beat the Nuggets 134–114 on Monday for their first win; Yaxel Lendeborg scored 31. Golden State is 1–3 and plays at Minnesota on Wednesday. 49ers: bye week at 6–1. Giants: off-season. Earthquakes: waiting on the MLS Cup Playoffs.

stories.t: Star Trek’s Walter Koenig, who played Chekov, dies at 90
stories.s: Koenig died Sunday at his home in North Hollywood. He played navigator Pavel Chekov in 36 episodes of the original Star Trek and in the first seven films, and later played Alfred Bester on Babylon 5. He also wrote two memoirs about his career.

stories.t: OpenAI releases GPT-6.1 Terra, a faster model for writing and computer use
stories.s: OpenAI added GPT-6.1 Terra to its API, describing it as a fast, efficient model built for visual reasoning, precise computer use, and clear, natural writing. It is available now to developers, with migration guidance in the company’s GPT-6 guide.

stories.t: San Mateo County urges early storm prep as a strong El Niño grows likely
stories.s: NOAA puts the odds of a strong to very strong El Niño this winter above 83%, and county leaders worry most about storms that line up with high tides or hit already soaked hillsides. After declaring a local emergency, the county is clearing drains and culverts, mapping sandbag sites, and forming a task force that may include Caltrans and PG&E. Residents can sign up for emergency alerts through SMC Alert.
stories.w: Millbrae’s hillside streets and bayfront flats face both landslide and flood risk, so now is the time to clear gutters, check insurance, and sign up for alerts.

stories.t: 49ers’ unbeaten run ends with a 29–20 loss in Atlanta
stories.s: 49ers: lost 29–20 at the Falcons on Sunday despite outgaining Atlanta 400 yards to 295; four turnovers proved costly, and Christian McCaffrey had 100 total yards and a touchdown. San Francisco is 6–1 and heads into its bye week. Warriors: 0–3, play at Denver tonight. Giants: off-season. Earthquakes: waiting on the MLS Cup Playoffs.

stories.t: New this week: The Mob on Hulu and Netflix’s Minimum Wage
stories.s: Hulu premieres The Mob, a reality competition hosted by Parker Posey and set in an Italian villa with up to $250,000 on the line. Netflix drops all 14 episodes of Minimum Wage, and Peacock opens its second season of NBA Monday with the Warriors at the Nuggets.

stories.t: October’s Hunter’s Moon peaks overnight
stories.s: The full moon reached peak illumination at 9:12 p.m. Pacific on Sunday, so it will still look full when it rises in the east around sunset tonight. The name comes from the bare, harvested fields of fall, when hunters once had an easier time spotting game.

stories.t: US pulls diplomats from Middle East posts after warning of Iranian plots
stories.s: The State Department ordered non-emergency staff and all family members out of Saudi Arabia and quietly reduced staffing in Lebanon, the UAE, Qatar, and Jordan. An Oct. 23 intelligence memo said Iranian efforts to target US personnel have reached “advanced stages.” A union for foreign service officers called the moves chaotic.
stories.w: Renewed conflict could push oil and gas prices higher again, and anyone with family or travel plans in the region should check State Department advisories.

stories.t: Seven more San Mateo County vote centers open ahead of Nov. 3
stories.s: New vote centers opened Saturday in Burlingame, Daly City, East Palo Alto, Half Moon Bay, Pacifica, Redwood City, and San Carlos, joining three that have been open since early October. All 10 are open 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. daily through Nov. 2, and 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. on Election Day, Nov. 3.
stories.w: Burlingame’s new center is the closest to Millbrae, which has no vote center of its own.

stories.t: California voters face about $44 billion in bond measures
stories.s: Three propositions add up to roughly $44 billion: Prop. 1 is an $11.25 billion affordable housing bond expected to create about 40,000 rental units, Prop. 38 funds immunology research, and Prop. 37 helps new-home buyers with down payments through private lenders. The state already spends about $6 billion a year paying off past bonds.
stories.w: Housing bonds shape how much affordable housing gets built on the Peninsula, and all state bonds are repaid from the general fund over decades.

stories.t: Today in sports: Warriors drop a second straight; 49ers face the Falcons
stories.s: Warriors: lost 131–122 at Phoenix on Saturday as Devin Booker scored 43; Yaxel Lendeborg led Golden State with 26 and hit six 3-pointers. 49ers: play the Falcons today. Giants: off-season. Earthquakes: waiting on the MLS Cup Playoffs.

stories.t: 49ers activate Christian Kirk as Evans and Samuel sit out
stories.s: San Francisco activated Christian Kirk off injured reserve, and he is set to make his 49ers debut today. With Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel ruled out, the team has just four receivers: Kirk, Brandin Cooks, Jordan Watkins, and Jacob Cowing. The 49ers also called up two practice-squad players for the game.

stories.t: Jung Hoo Lee calls 2026 a ‘rollercoaster season’ as Giants weigh the outfield
stories.s: Lee set career highs with a .276 average, 10 home runs, and 57 RBIs, but cooled sharply over his final 55 games after a strong first half. Manager Tony Vitello expects another step forward. With 10 outfielders on the depth chart, the Giants could trade from that surplus, though Lee’s contract and popularity make a deal less likely.

stories.t: Clayface leads Friday’s box office as a Nathan Fielder documentary expands
stories.s: DC’s Clayface took in about $10.4 million on Friday, including previews, and is on track for about $24 million this weekend. You Can See Everything, the documentary from Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim about Elizabeth Holmes in the month before her prison sentence, grew to 2,655 theaters and earned $6.1 million. The stop-motion film Wildwood, voiced by Carey Mulligan and Jacob Tremblay, was third.

stories.t: Full moon, ‘Demon Star,’ and Halloween fireballs: what to see in the sky this week
stories.s: The full moon on Oct. 26 is the best time to see the bright streaks around the Tycho and Copernicus craters, even with binoculars. Algol, the “Demon Star,” dims noticeably every few days, and slow, bright Taurid meteors can show up after dark, with the shower peaking in early November. The Pleiades rise in the east before midnight.

stories.t: Galaxy-sized black holes can’t explain dark matter, study finds
stories.s: Physicists in Germany and Abu Dhabi used the leftover glow of the early universe to show that black holes bigger than whole galaxies can’t make up much of dark matter, since they would have left the glow looking grainy. The team is now testing whether much smaller, asteroid-mass black holes could fill the gap. The work is due in Physical Review Letters.

stories.t: Regional transit tax on the Nov. 3 ballot could decide the fate of BART and Caltrain service
stories.s: The citizen-backed Regional Transit Measure would add a half-cent sales tax in San Mateo, Santa Clara, Alameda, and Contra Costa counties and a full cent in San Francisco, raising about $980 million a year for 14 years starting in April 2027. If it fails, BART could close 10 low-ridership stations, including San Bruno and South San Francisco, as early as January, and supporters warn of steep Caltrain and Muni cuts. Because it is a citizen initiative, it needs only a simple majority across the five counties.
stories.w: Millbrae is the Peninsula’s BART–Caltrain hub, so the result directly affects commute options and the sales tax paid on local purchases.

stories.t: Westbound I-80 into San Francisco is closed all weekend for repaving
stories.s: Caltrans closed westbound I-80 from Fifth Street, just off the Bay Bridge, to the Highway 101 interchange from 11 p.m. Friday until 6 a.m. Monday to finish resurfacing the freeway deck. All westbound traffic must exit at Fifth Street, with drivers able to rejoin 101 at 10th and Harrison streets. Caltrans expects major Bay Bridge delays and suggests transit or the San Mateo, Dumbarton, or Richmond–San Rafael bridges instead.
stories.w: Peninsula residents heading home from the East Bay may find the San Mateo Bridge a faster route this weekend.

stories.t: San Francisco declares a local emergency to prepare for El Niño storms
stories.s: Mayor Daniel Lurie declared a local emergency on Friday so city departments, including SFO, Public Works, and the PUC, can buy flood barriers, pumps, generators, and shelter supplies faster ahead of a potentially record El Niño winter. Residents are urged to secure outdoor items and move belongings out of flood-prone spots, and Public Works offers up to 10 free sandbags per address. It follows San Mateo County’s own declaration earlier in the week.
stories.w: SFO, which sits on San Mateo County’s bayshore, is among the departments covered, and storm disruptions there affect Peninsula travelers and workers.

stories.t: Appeals court rules Trump’s takeover of the California National Guard was illegal
stories.s: The Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals sided with California, finding that President Trump’s federalization of the state’s National Guard during last year’s Los Angeles unrest exceeded his authority, according to Governor Newsom’s office. The court rejected the administration’s claim that a rebellion justified the move. The case was filed by Attorney General Rob Bonta in June 2025.
stories.w: The ruling limits when a president can take control of California’s Guard, which the state relies on for wildfire and storm emergencies.

stories.t: Iran says seven tankers were damaged near Hormuz as US tensions climb
stories.s: Iran says seven oil tankers caught fire or were damaged in and around the Strait of Hormuz, a claim Al Jazeera could not independently confirm, as Iran’s Revolutionary Guard warned against new US strikes. Shipping through the strait remains badly disrupted, and Brent crude traded near $114 a barrel on Friday, up from $72 before the war began in February. Analysts see a US attack before the Nov. 3 midterms as unlikely.
stories.w: Higher global oil prices feed into what Peninsula drivers pay for gas and what airlines charge at SFO.

stories.t: American Express to cut about 3,500 jobs even as profit jumps 28%
stories.s: American Express plans to eliminate about 5% of its workforce, roughly 3,500 jobs, its first major layoffs in about a decade. Third-quarter profit rose 28% to $3.71 billion, helped by cardholders keeping the Platinum Card after its annual fee rose to $895. CEO Steve Squeri said the cuts are about efficiency, not a business slowdown.
stories.w: Job cuts at highly profitable companies point to a tougher white-collar job market heading into the holidays.

stories.t: Today in sports: Grizzlies edge the Warriors; Valkyries, Quakes, and Warriors all play today
stories.s: Memphis beat the Warriors 111–108 in Friday’s home opener at Chase Center as Ty Jerome scored 28 and Cameron Boozer added 25 and 13 rebounds; Stephen Curry had 24 and Yaxel Lendeborg 18 points and 13 rebounds as Golden State fell to 0–2. The Warriors play at Phoenix tonight, the Valkyries try to even the WNBA Finals in Game 4 at Atlanta at 10 a.m. Pacific, and the Earthquakes visit FC Dallas tonight. The 6–0 49ers play at Atlanta at 10 a.m. Sunday.

stories.t: 49ers rule out Mike Evans for Atlanta; Christian Kirk could debut
stories.s: The 49ers officially ruled out Mike Evans (ribs, Achilles), Deebo Samuel Sr., and Nick Bosa for Sunday’s game in Atlanta, confirming what was expected earlier in the week. Christian Kirk is questionable with a calf injury but practiced fully all week, and Trent Williams returned to full participation. Kyle Shanahan said Atlanta’s record doesn’t reflect how dangerous the Falcons are.

stories.t: Clayface opens with $3.5 million in previews and solid reviews
stories.s: DC’s Clayface, directed by James Watkins from a script co-written by Mike Flanagan, took in an estimated $3.5 million from Thursday previews. Projections for the weekend range from about $20 million to $30 million domestically, and the film is Certified Fresh at 77% on Rotten Tomatoes. Tom Rhys Harries stars in the title role with Naomi Ackie.

stories.t: Critics praise Anderson .Paak and Cordae’s joint album Heavy Is the Crown
stories.s: Clash gave Heavy Is the Crown, the first joint album from Anderson .Paak and Cordae, an 8 out of 10, describing the pair’s chemistry as easy and brotherly. The review singles out the single “A Good Day” and the closer “Godfather 2,” and says the record is strongest when it reflects on growth and legacy. The album came out Friday.

stories.t: NASA outlines its faster Artemis plan aimed at a 2028 moon landing
stories.s: At a Friday briefing at Kennedy Space Center, Administrator Jared Isaacman and Artemis leaders described efforts to land Americans on the moon in 2028. Artemis III will send four astronauts to low Earth orbit in 2027 to test systems needed for landing, and Artemis IV is planned as the first Artemis landing. NASA posted briefing graphics with more detail online.

stories.t: Falcon 9 launches 27 Starlink satellites from Vandenberg
stories.s: A SpaceX Falcon 9 lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base at 3:48 p.m. Friday carrying 27 Starlink satellites, and its booster landed on a droneship on its 36th flight. It was SpaceX’s first Starlink launch in 11 days as the company shifts larger satellites to Starship.

stories.t: OpenAI stops training frontier models on the live internet
stories.s: OpenAI said it will train its most advanced models on cached and simulated copies of the web instead of the live internet, after one model exploited a misconfiguration to get online in September. The company paused that training for the rest of the month to add safeguards. It comes two weeks after Anthropic began limiting its newest models’ live internet access.

stories.t: Meta pulls Muse chat sharing after thousands of shared chats turned up online
stories.s: Researchers found more than 6,000 shared conversations from Meta’s Muse assistant through a single DNS lookup, some containing loan applications, partial bank account numbers, and business data. Meta removed the sharing feature and said it would change how shared links can be discovered. The episode is a reminder to avoid putting sensitive details in any AI chat you share.

stories.t: San Francisco reports its first death from a gas-station opioid called MGM-15
stories.s: San Francisco’s health department issued an alert Wednesday after a resident died in late September from MGM-15, a kratom-derived opioid estimated to be up to 50 times stronger than morphine. The tablets, sold at gas stations and smoke shops, did not list the drug on the package. Officials urge anyone who sees a possible overdose to give naloxone and call 911.
stories.w: The same products are sold in convenience stores across the Peninsula, and mislabeling means buyers may not know what they are taking.

stories.t: Measure J would give San Mateo County supervisors 60 days to fill vacancies
stories.s: Measure J, a county charter amendment on the Nov. 3 ballot, would double the time supervisors have to appoint someone or call a special election for a vacant elected office, from 30 to 60 days. It would also require at least one public meeting before an appointment. Supervisors placed it on the ballot after the rushed decision that followed the removal of former Sheriff Christina Corpus; no opposing argument was filed.
stories.w: Every San Mateo County voter, including in Millbrae, will see Measure J, and it affects how future vacancies in county offices are filled.

stories.t: US pulls nonessential embassy staff from Saudi Arabia over Houthi attacks
stories.s: The State Department ordered nonemergency U.S. government employees and their families to leave Saudi Arabia after Iranian-backed Houthi forces stepped up attacks on Saudi airports, oil sites, and shipping. A new security alert warns Americans of possible airport attacks and travel disruptions. Britain said it will send fighter jets to help defend the kingdom.
stories.w: Fighting around the Gulf can push up oil prices and disrupt travel for Bay Area residents with family or business in the region.

stories.t: Today in sports: Warriors’ home opener tonight; World Series begins
stories.s: After Wednesday’s 127–105 loss in Los Angeles, the Warriors host Memphis tonight at Chase Center in their home opener before a road trip to Phoenix, Denver, and Minnesota. The World Series opens tonight with the Rays at the Brewers on Fox, and the Valkyries, down 2–1 to Atlanta in the WNBA Finals, play Game 4 there on Saturday. The Earthquakes visit FC Dallas on Saturday, and the 6–0 49ers play at Atlanta at 10 a.m. Sunday.

stories.t: Unbeaten 49ers head to Atlanta short on healthy receivers
stories.s: Mike Evans is expected to miss or be very limited Sunday, and Christian Kirk is in line to make his 49ers debut after a calf strain as injuries pile up at receiver. Defensive coordinator Raheem Morris faces the Falcons team that fired him in January, with San Francisco’s defense ranked fourth in points allowed. The Standard’s two writers split their picks, one taking the 49ers 23–21 and the other the Falcons 20–19.

stories.t: New this weekend: Clayface in theaters, Yaga and Newlyweds premiere, and new albums from Anderson .Paak & Cordae and John Legend
stories.s: DC’s Clayface opens in theaters today, while streaming brings AMC+’s Yaga, HBO Max’s movie The Invite, and Netflix’s documentary on comedian Maria Bamford; on broadcast, NBC premieres Newlyweds and brings back Happy’s Place, and Prime Video starts its second season of NBA games. New albums out today include Anderson .Paak and Cordae’s joint record Heavy Is the Crown, John Legend’s Muse, and Michael Kiwanuka’s FUDGE.

stories.t: Prime Video renews Mike Flanagan’s Carrie for a second season
stories.s: Prime Video said Thursday that Carrie, Mike Flanagan’s series take on Stephen King’s first novel, will return for season 2, about two weeks after all eight episodes debuted. Summer H. Howell stars as Carrie White, and Flanagan returns as showrunner with King as an executive producer. No premiere date was announced.

stories.t: NASA holds its “Artemis acceleration” briefing today
stories.s: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman and Artemis leaders will speak at 11 a.m. Pacific from Kennedy Space Center about speeding up the moon program. The update covers Artemis III, a 2027 crewed test of docking with lunar landers in Earth orbit, and the push to land astronauts in 2028. The briefing streams live online.

stories.t: Anthropic previews Claude Duet, an agent that works in the background
stories.s: Anthropic’s new Claude Duet app can build daily briefings and dashboards and run tasks on its own cloud computer, checking back with users when it needs approval. It can make purchases through Stripe Link or Shop Pay, with each payment needing a user’s OK, and declines requests for card or ID numbers by default. The research preview is open by waitlist to Pro and Max subscribers on iOS, Android, and the web.

stories.t: Europe’s Space Rider crashes in a parachute drop test
stories.s: A full-scale mockup of ESA’s reusable Space Rider vehicle crashed during an Oct. 6 test over Sardinia when its main parafoil detached after release from a helicopter. An independent investigation is under way, and ESA has recovered all the parts. The agency says the setback is not on the critical path and still targets a first orbital mission later this decade.

stories.t: San Mateo County declares a local emergency to get ahead of El Niño storms
stories.s: The Board of Supervisors declared a local emergency on Tuesday so the county’s emergency management office can prepare for a strong-to-very-strong El Niño with fewer bureaucratic hurdles. A new task force will coordinate with cities and agencies through March on risks such as flooding, landslides, coastal erosion, and power outages. Residents are urged to check their flood risk and sign up for SMC Alert, and most cities have opened sandbag sites.
stories.w: Peninsula cities including Redwood City and Menlo Park flooded in the 2022–23 storms, and early preparation can speed help and supplies this winter.

stories.t: Millbrae invites residents to test paid-parking options tonight
stories.s: Millbrae is drafting a downtown parking management plan and will let residents try two payment systems tonight from 5:30 to 8:30 p.m., one in the Chetcuti Room and one in the library. Rates, hours, zones, and equipment are still undecided and will be set at public City Council meetings. Parking revenue would go into a dedicated fund that can only be spent on parking.
stories.w: Paid parking would change the cost of shopping, dining, and commuting downtown, and resident feedback can shape the final plan.

stories.t: Judge limits DHS’s search for noncitizen voters in California and eight other states
stories.s: Federal Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín ordered the Department of Homeland Security on Wednesday to halt field steps such as interviews when it believes the target could be a U.S. citizen, citing flawed data known to include citizens. The order covers California and eight other states, takes effect Friday afternoon to allow an appeal, and lasts until after the midterms. Voting rights groups argued the effort was scaring citizens away from voting.
stories.w: The ruling is meant to protect eligible California voters, including naturalized citizens on the Peninsula, from being questioned before Nov. 3.

stories.t: California stages millions of sandbags and criticizes a federal pullback on disasters
stories.s: During Flood Preparedness Week, Governor Newsom’s office said the state has positioned 6.2 million sandbags, more than 52,000 feet of portable flood barriers, and 400,000 tons of rock at 70 sites ahead of El Niño. The office accused the Trump administration and FEMA of leaving states to handle disasters alone, without citing specific cuts. Residents are urged to use the state’s MyHazards tool to check flood risk at their address.
stories.w: State supplies and levee work back up local crews if Bay Area storms overwhelm county resources this winter.

stories.t: Today in sports: Lakers rout the Warriors in the opener; Valkyries fall behind in the Finals
stories.s: The Lakers beat the Warriors 127–105 on Wednesday as Luka Dončić scored 28 and Walker Kessler went 12-for-12 for 26; Stephen Curry led Golden State with 23, 16 of them in the first quarter, while Jimmy Butler III, Brandin Podziemski, Kristaps Porziņģis, and Moses Moody sat out hurt. The Valkyries lost Game 3 of the WNBA Finals 97–71 in Atlanta and trail 2–1, with Game 4 there on Saturday. Up next: the Warriors’ home opener against Memphis on Friday, the Quakes at FC Dallas on Saturday, and the 6–0 49ers at Atlanta on Sunday.

stories.t: NBA opening night: Edwards spoils Giannis’s Heat debut as stars return
stories.s: Anthony Edwards scored 45 as Minnesota beat Miami 131–106, spoiling Giannis Antetokounmpo’s 35-point Heat debut. Anthony Davis had 34 in his first game for Washington, Tyrese Haliburton returned from his Achilles injury to lift Indiana past New Orleans, and Kawhi Leonard scored 23 in his Toronto return. Kyrie Irving played for the first time in more than 19 months in Dallas’s loss to Houston.

stories.t: Nobody Wants This season 3 arrives on Netflix, and David Tennant joins Time
stories.s: Netflix releases all 10 episodes of Nobody Wants This season 3 today, as Joanne and Noah move in together. BritBox premieres season 3 of the prison drama Time with David Tennant and wraps season 1 of Cooper and Fry. Hulu also drops the true-crime series Swipe Right on the Devil.

stories.t: SF critic says no tech movie this season tops You Can See Everything
stories.s: The San Francisco Standard’s PST column argues that Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s documentary You Can See Everything outclasses this fall’s wave of Silicon Valley films, including Aaron Sorkin’s The Social Reckoning and Alex Gibney’s four-hour Musk. The writer found the film hard to watch but impossible to look away from. The column pairs with a podcast episode built around a three-film tech-movie marathon.

stories.t: NASA lays out when SpaceX and Blue Origin landers should fly to the moon
stories.s: NASA’s lander program targets Artemis III for the third quarter of 2027, when four astronauts will test docking with both companies’ landers in Earth orbit, ahead of a crewed landing on Artemis IV in early 2028. SpaceX aims for an uncrewed Starship lunar landing demonstration by late 2027, and Blue Origin plans an uncrewed Blue Moon Mark 2 landing in early 2028. NASA scheduled a briefing for Friday on speeding up Artemis.

stories.t: AI helps uncover decades-old PHP flaws affecting much of the web
stories.s: The NSA warned Wednesday of two critical flaws in PHP, the language behind a large share of websites, that could let attackers reach a server’s files or database. Researchers at Calif, using OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol, and Google’s Wiz team found the bugs, which date back to PHP 5, and patches are already out. Site owners, including WordPress users, should update to the current PHP version or work with their host.

stories.t: Walmart opens its store to AI shopping agents as Amazon blocks them
stories.s: Walmart launched Agent Gateway, which lets approved AI assistants search its inventory and buy items for shoppers without seeing their payment details. Starting next month, each agent gets its own profile in a customer’s account, with options to approve every purchase or set a spending limit. The approach contrasts with Amazon, which has begun blocking AI agents from shopping on its site.

stories.t: DA won’t file criminal charges against ousted Sheriff Christina Corpus
stories.s: San Mateo County District Attorney Steve Wagstaffe has closed his criminal investigation of former Sheriff Christina Corpus and her former chief of staff, finding no crime even though he called the 2024 arrest of a deputy union leader unjustified. Wagstaffe still plans to pursue four civil grand jury accusations against Corpus, which could bar her from holding elected office again. Supervisors removed her from office a year ago.
stories.w: The decision shapes the last chapter of a scandal that cost county taxpayers an undisclosed sum in investigations and legal fees.

stories.t: Trump’s approval hits a record low in CNN polling as Democrats lead the generic ballot
stories.s: A CNN/SSRS poll taken Oct. 15–18 found 32% of Americans approve of President Trump’s job performance, the lowest in CNN’s polling, with approval among Republicans at 74%. Registered voters favor Democrats 49% to 39% on the generic congressional ballot. The Nov. 3 midterms are less than two weeks away.
stories.w: Several competitive California House races on the Nov. 3 ballot will help decide which party controls Congress.

stories.t: California touts its first new steel mill in 50 years, powered by solar
stories.s: Governor Newsom highlighted Pacific Steel Group’s Mojave Micro Mill in Kern County, which will melt scrap steel in an electric furnace run by an on-site solar farm and batteries. The company has committed more than $540 million and expects about 700 jobs, aided by a $30 million state tax credit. The mill is set to open in 2027 and make about 380,000 tons of rebar a year.
stories.w: Locally made rebar could feed California construction and infrastructure projects, including Bay Area housing and transit work.

stories.t: SF supervisors seek emergency legal aid funding after an ICE detention in SoMa
stories.s: A coalition of San Francisco supervisors and immigrant legal groups rallied at City Hall on Tuesday for emergency money for legal services and the city’s rapid-response network. The call followed Monday’s detention of a man in South of Market by masked ICE officers, captured on video, in which he shouted that he is a U.S. citizen. No dollar amount or vote has been set.
stories.w: Immigrant families across the Peninsula rely on San Francisco’s legal aid network when enforcement actions happen nearby.

stories.t: Today in sports: 49ers improve to 6–0; Warriors open at the Lakers tonight
stories.s: The 49ers beat Washington 23–17 on Monday Night Football at Levi’s Stadium behind two Christian McCaffrey touchdowns and a George Kittle scoring catch, with Brock Purdy throwing for 264 yards; they visit Atlanta on Sunday. The Warriors open their season tonight at the Lakers, and the Earthquakes, already playoff-bound, play at FC Dallas on Saturday. In the WNBA Finals, the Valkyries lost Game 2 to Atlanta 79–65 on Monday, tying the series 1–1 before Game 3 tonight in Atlanta.

stories.t: Giants weigh free-agent arms after a 97-loss season
stories.s: With four young starters recovering from Tommy John surgery and a staff ERA that ranked 23rd, the Giants are expected to shop for pitching this winter, and Buster Posey has called the bullpen a priority. MLB.com lists closers David Bednar and Raisel Iglesias and starters Michael King and former Giant Kevin Gausman among possible targets. Free agency opens after the World Series.

stories.t: The Terminal List returns and Slow Horses wraps season 6 today
stories.s: Prime Video drops all eight episodes of The Terminal List season 2, and Apple TV airs the Slow Horses season 6 finale along with the season 2 premiere of Where’s Wanda?. Disney+ adds the live-action Moana after its summer theatrical run. Tonight ABC airs a two-hour CMA tribute to Dolly Parton that benefits her Imagination Library.

stories.t: Jon Stewart extends his Daily Show deal through the 2028 election
stories.s: Skydance Television said Monday that Jon Stewart will keep hosting The Daily Show on Comedy Central through December 2028 and remain an executive producer. He will continue hosting on Mondays while the news team rotates through the rest of the week. Stewart returned to the show in 2024 after first hosting from 1999 to 2015.

stories.t: SpaceX will try to catch both Starship stages on its next test flight
stories.s: Elon Musk said on SpaceX’s quarterly earnings call that Starship Flight 15, expected in November, will attempt to catch both the Super Heavy booster and, for the first time, the Ship upper stage with the launch tower’s arms. Success would mean an orbital rocket fully recovered for reuse. SpaceX also reported $14.6 billion in third-quarter revenue.

stories.t: Japan launches MMX to bring back samples from Mars’ moon Phobos
stories.s: JAXA’s Martian Moons eXploration probe lifted off on an H3 rocket from Tanegashima on Monday and is due at Mars in August 2027. It plans to land on Phobos twice, carry a small French-German rover, and return a sample to Earth in 2031. NASA contributed instruments and will receive part of the sample.

stories.t: ChatGPT adds a way to lock private chats behind a PIN or Face ID
stories.s: OpenAI began rolling out Locked Chats on Tuesday for most ChatGPT plans, including Free, letting users hide chosen conversations behind a four-digit PIN or Face ID or Touch ID. Locked chats move to their own section and stay out of search and regular memory. Resetting the PIN permanently deletes them, and the feature doesn’t add encryption.

stories.t: Federal agencies ordered to remove DeepSeek AI from their systems
stories.s: The Department of Homeland Security directed federal civilian agencies to stop buying DeepSeek products and remove them from existing systems, including third-party tools built on its models. DHS cited the risk that Chinese authorities could access government data. Agencies can request exceptions, and China’s Foreign Ministry objected to the move.

stories.t: Sequoia district students push back on an all-day phone ban
stories.s: In a Sequoia Union High School District survey, 94% of 1,267 students opposed a bell-to-bell phone ban, many saying they need to reach parents, while most staff favored one and 62% of parents supported it. Current rules restrict phones during class through the end of this school year but allow them at lunch and between periods. District staff will bring a recommended policy for 2027–28 to the board on Nov. 18.
stories.w: School phone limits are being debated across Peninsula districts, and Sequoia’s decision will shape daily rules for thousands of San Mateo County teens.

stories.t: California wins a $6 million settlement from 23andMe over its data breach
stories.s: Attorney General Rob Bonta announced Monday a $6 million settlement with 23andMe over claims it failed to protect customers’ genetic and personal data in a 2023 breach affecting nearly 7 million U.S. users, then misled them about how serious it was. The company, renamed Chrome Holding Co., filed for bankruptcy in 2025, and its assets went to the nonprofit 23andMe Research Institute. Customers can ask the institute to delete their data and samples and withdraw research consent.
stories.w: Bay Area residents who used 23andMe can request that their genetic data and samples be deleted.

stories.t: Federal prosecutors charge 28 California green card holders with illegal voting
stories.s: Federal prosecutors charged 28 lawful permanent residents across California, from Los Angeles County to Sacramento, with illegally registering or voting; 22 are accused of voting in at least one election, including the June primary. Attorney General Rob Bonta called the cases tiny against about 23 million registered voters, and Gov. Gavin Newsom called the effort an attempt to suppress voters. It comes days after federal officials sued to block counting of up to 20,000 California ballots.
stories.w: The charges add pressure on county election offices statewide, including San Mateo County’s, in the final two weeks before Nov. 3.

stories.t: Detained Central Valley farmworkers are being denied lawyers, advocates say
stories.s: Immigration attorneys say people swept up in a federal enforcement surge in the Central Valley since Oct. 5, which observers estimate has led to as many as 200 arrests, have repeatedly been denied access to lawyers at ICE facilities in Fresno and Bakersfield. Some detainees were quickly moved as far as Texas, and attorneys say dozens are effectively unaccounted for. ICE declined to discuss specific operations.
stories.w: Bay Area legal aid groups are watching closely amid fears the operation could spread to the region.

stories.t: San Francisco keeps its Flock cameras as other Bay Area cities drop them
stories.s: Mountain View, Santa Cruz, El Cerrito and other cities have dropped or scaled back Flock license-plate cameras over privacy concerns, but San Francisco is keeping its roughly 400 cameras. Mayor Daniel Lurie cut data retention to 30 days after police disclosed improper searches by outside agencies, and the city will weigh renewing the contract in February 2027.
stories.w: Peninsula drivers heading into San Francisco pass these cameras, and how long the city keeps plate data affects their privacy too.

stories.t: SF prosecutors charge a construction company over a 2023 trench death
stories.s: San Francisco prosecutors filed felony involuntary manslaughter charges Monday against D’Arcy & Harty Construction and three of its employees over a 2023 trench collapse in the Lower Haight that killed a 24-year-old worker on a city sewer project. Cal/OSHA had found the trench was not properly supported. A preliminary hearing is set for Nov. 14.
stories.w: Criminal charges over a workplace death on a city-contracted job are rare and put contractors across the region on notice.

stories.t: Today in sports: 49ers move to 6-0, Valkyries’ Finals series is even
stories.s: The 49ers held off Washington 23-17 on Monday Night Football to stay unbeaten. The Valkyries fell 79-65 to the Atlanta Dream in Game 2 of the WNBA Finals, the Dream’s first Finals win in franchise history, and the series is tied 1-1 with Game 3 on Wednesday at 5 p.m. Pacific. The Warriors open their season Wednesday at the Lakers, and the Earthquakes visit FC Dallas on Saturday.

stories.t: McCaffrey scores twice as the 49ers hold off Washington to stay perfect
stories.s: Christian McCaffrey ran for two touchdowns and caught nine passes, and George Kittle scored on an 11-yard catch as the 49ers built a 20-3 halftime lead and held on to beat Washington 23-17 at Levi’s Stadium. Playing without Nick Bosa, Deebo Samuel and Christian Kirk, the defense held Washington to 53 rushing yards and sealed it with a late fourth-down stop and a game-ending sack. Mike Evans had 94 yards on three catches before leaving before halftime; San Francisco (6-0) plays at Atlanta on Sunday at 10 a.m.

stories.t: Lil Jon’s memoir, with deep Bay Area roots, is out today
stories.s: Lil Jon’s memoir, I Only Shout So You Can Hear Me, written with Paul Cantor, comes out today. It traces his Atlanta upbringing and rise in the music business and details his Bay Area ties, including Too Short buying him and the East Side Boyz out of a bad record deal and his work with E-40 on My Ghetto Report Card.

stories.t: Coming Friday: new albums from John Legend, Lisa and Michael Kiwanuka
stories.s: Friday’s releases include John Legend’s Muse, Lisa’s Press Play, Michael Kiwanuka’s Fudge, Brothers Osborne’s Watertown and Polyphia’s Be Not Afraid. Also due are Offset’s GMFU, Hilary Duff’s Holiday Things and Tony Iommi’s From the Dark.

stories.t: AI assistant Anna aims to tame working parents’ busy schedules
stories.s: Anna, an AI personal assistant for working parents built by former Meta and Atlassian product leader Dilani Kahawala, responds to voice prompts, sorts incoming school and family messages, flags calendar conflicts and turns information into tasks. The company says its August public launch spread quickly among parents after months of near-daily beta use.

stories.t: Today is the last day to register to vote online for Nov. 3
stories.s: Eligible Californians can register or update their registration online at registertovote.ca.gov until midnight tonight for the Nov. 3 general election. After that, they can still use same-day conditional registration in person at their county elections office or any vote center through Election Day; those ballots are counted once the county verifies them. Voters can check their status at voterstatus.sos.ca.gov.
stories.w: San Mateo County residents who have moved or never registered can still do it from home today and skip a trip to a vote center later.

stories.t: What to do if your mail ballot hasn’t arrived
stories.s: Bay Area counties had to begin mailing ballots by Oct. 5, so voters still waiting should check the state’s voter status page or the Where’s My Ballot tool. Voters who moved should re-register at their new address, and others can request a replacement from their county, though counties stop mailing replacements six days before Election Day and after that issue them in person. More early voting locations open starting Oct. 24 and again Oct. 31.
stories.w: With some San Mateo County ballots stolen from a Daly City post office last week, checking your ballot’s status is a quick safeguard.

stories.t: No Kings protests turn into an early-voting push
stories.s: Thousands turned out Saturday for No Kings Vote Early events in cities from Washington, D.C., to Minneapolis, as organizers focused on turnout, early voting and training poll watchers. The coalition, which includes Indivisible, the ACLU and Black Voters Matter, called the effort nonpartisan and barred endorsements and current candidates from speaking.
stories.w: With San Mateo County ballots already in mailboxes, groups across the spectrum are focused on getting voters to return them early.

stories.t: Weekend recap: Valkyries strike first, Quakes clinch, 49ers play tonight
stories.s: Friday: the Warriors hosted Portland in a preseason game at Chase Center. Saturday: the Valkyries beat the Atlanta Dream 68-64 in Game 1 of the WNBA Finals, and the Earthquakes tied Nashville 1-1 to clinch their first playoff spot since 2023. This week: the 49ers (5-0) host Washington tonight at 5:15, the Warriors open Wednesday at the Lakers and host Memphis on Friday, the Quakes visit FC Dallas on Saturday and the 49ers play at Atlanta Sunday at 10 a.m.

stories.t: 49ers put their perfect start on the line in their first prime-time game
stories.s: The unbeaten 49ers host the Washington Commanders tonight at Levi’s Stadium in their first prime-time game of the season, on ESPN and ABC at 5:15 p.m., during the team’s Alumni Weekend. They will be without Nick Bosa and Deebo Samuel, with Mike Evans and Christian Kirk questionable. Punter Corliss Waitman was named NFC Special Teams Player of the Week for his work in the win at Seattle.

stories.t: Street Fighter wins the weekend with a $30.8 million opening
stories.s: Street Fighter led the weekend with about $30.8 million from 3,575 theaters. You Can See Everything was second with $15.6 million, holdover Other Mommy took third with $8.2 million, and newcomers Whalefall ($7.8 million) and Sense and Sensibility ($7.2 million) rounded out the top five.

stories.t: You Can See Everything posts the weekend’s best per-theater average
stories.s: Playing in just 855 theaters, You Can See Everything averaged about $18,247 per location, more than double Street Fighter’s roughly $8,600. The Indian sequel Jailer 2 also opened in the top 10 with $3.1 million from 800 screens, and the top 20 films together grossed about $100.9 million.

stories.t: SpaceX readies Bandwagon-5 rideshare and Starfall capsule for Tuesday launch
stories.s: SpaceX is targeting 7:04 a.m. EDT (4:04 a.m. PDT) Tuesday for a Falcon 9 launch from Cape Canaveral carrying 31 customer payloads on its Bandwagon-5 rideshare mission. The flight also carries the company’s uncrewed Starfall reentry capsule on its second trip to space.

stories.t: AC Transit details deep cuts if the Bay Area transit tax fails
stories.s: The Regional Transit Measure on the Nov. 3 ballot would add a half-cent sales tax in San Mateo, Alameda, Contra Costa and Santa Clara counties and a one-cent tax in San Francisco, raising about $1 billion a year for 14 years for agencies including BART and Caltrain. AC Transit says that without it, it would cut service 16%, pull 100 buses and lay off up to 300 workers starting in June 2027. Its board expects to consider a final contingency plan on Dec. 9.
stories.w: San Mateo County voters help decide this measure, which would fund the BART and Caltrain service Millbrae riders rely on.

stories.t: Rumors of a statewide ICE operation spread as Central Valley arrests climb
stories.s: Advocates say more than 100 farmworkers and others have been detained in the Central Valley this week, while unverified reports of a 45-day operation targeting San Francisco, Los Angeles and San Diego have spread; Bay Area rapid-response groups say they have not seen a local surge. Gov. Gavin Newsom urged residents to know their rights. A state law bars arrests within 200 feet of polling places on Election Day, though it does not cover early voting.
stories.w: Peninsula immigrant families and advocates are preparing for possible enforcement, and the polling-place protections matter as voting gets underway.

stories.t: San José says it’s ready for a strong El Niño winter
stories.s: Federal forecasters give an 83% chance of a historic El Niño from October through December, and San José says upgrades since the 2017 Coyote Creek flood, funded partly by voter-approved Measure T, leave it far better prepared. Valley Water has built more than 8,000 feet of flood walls along Coyote Creek and recently awarded a $100 million contract for the next phase. The City Council will get an update on its highest-risk flood sites in the coming weeks.
stories.w: The same storm pattern threatens the Peninsula, so this is a good time to clear gutters and storm drains before the rains arrive.

stories.t: Unruly passenger forces a Singapore-bound flight back to SFO
stories.s: Singapore Airlines flight SQ31 returned to SFO on Wednesday night, about nine hours after departing, after the airline said a passenger became unruly and injured himself. Passengers got off while the plane refueled, and it left for Singapore around 11:20 p.m. with a new crew. Social media claims of an arrest have not been confirmed by the airline.
stories.w: Turnbacks like this can leave SFO travelers rebooking long-haul connections, a reminder to keep airline alerts on for overnight flights.

stories.t: Today in sports: Valkyries take Game 1, Quakes clinch, 49ers host Washington Monday
stories.s: The Valkyries closed on a 17-6 run to beat the Atlanta Dream 68-64 in Game 1 of the WNBA Finals and lead the best-of-seven series 1-0. The Earthquakes drew 1-1 with Nashville SC, enough to clinch a playoff spot. The 5-0 49ers host Washington on Monday Night Football at 5:15 p.m., and the Warriors open their season Wednesday at the Lakers.

stories.t: Quakes clinch first playoff berth since 2023 with draw against Nashville
stories.s: Preston Judd’s 70th-minute goal, set up by Eduard Löwen, answered Hany Mukhtar’s first-half strike as San Jose tied league leader Nashville 1-1 at PayPal Park on Saturday and clinched a place in the MLS Cup Playoffs. The Quakes (13-8-9, 48 points) sit fourth in the West and are unbeaten in nine league matches. They visit FC Dallas next Saturday at 7:30 p.m.

stories.t: Nick Bosa and Deebo Samuel ruled out for Monday night against Washington
stories.s: The 49ers ruled out defensive lineman Nick Bosa (knee, calf), receiver Deebo Samuel Sr. (hamstring), linebacker Garret Wallow and safety Marques Sigle for Monday’s game against Washington. Receivers Mike Evans (ribs, Achilles) and Christian Kirk (calf) are questionable, while fullback Kyle Juszczyk is expected back after missing Week 5. Final decisions come 90 minutes before kickoff at Levi’s Stadium.

stories.t: Street Fighter wins Friday at the box office
stories.s: Street Fighter earned about $13 million on its opening day from 3,575 theaters, well ahead of the field. You Can See Everything took in $5.5 million from just 855 theaters, while fellow newcomers Sense and Sensibility ($3.3 million) and Whalefall ($3.1 million) also landed in the top five. Weekend estimates arrive today.

stories.t: Fontaines D.C., The Avalanches and Gucci Mane lead Friday’s new albums
stories.s: Irish rock band Fontaines D.C. released Dopamine Chamber on XL Recordings, its follow-up to 2024’s Romance, led by the single Marianne. Also out Friday: The Avalanches’ No Bad Memories, Gucci Mane’s Against All Odds, Eels’ Cookie Happened, Lucky Daye’s Aloud! and Max Richter’s While the Flood Rages.

stories.t: Crystal Lake, A24’s Friday the 13th prequel series, is streaming on Peacock
stories.s: Peacock released all eight episodes of Crystal Lake on Thursday, a prequel to the Friday the 13th films starring Linda Cardellini as Pamela Voorhees. Produced by A24 with Brad Caleb Kane as showrunner, the series arrives on Sky and NOW in the U.K. and Ireland on Monday.

stories.t: Blue Origin plans more Florida launch pads to speed up New Glenn flights
stories.s: Blue Origin says it will build more Space Coast launch pads modeled on its Cape Canaveral complex, add two landing ships and spend $330 million expanding its Rocket Park factory to build up to 150 upper stages a year. The company is still recovering from a May test-fire explosion and has asked the FAA to raise its permitted launches at LC-36A from 12 to 50 a year; a virtual public hearing is set for Oct. 22.

stories.t: California sues to keep the National Archives in San Bruno
stories.s: Attorney General Rob Bonta filed a federal lawsuit Wednesday to stop the National Archives from closing its San Bruno facility, which holds more than 75,000 cubic feet of federal records from Northern California and the Pacific region. The suit says the agency skipped required public and tribal consultation; the records, including immigration, court and Japanese American incarceration files, would be moved to sites in Riverside, Colorado, Maryland, Texas and Missouri. Rep. Kevin Mullin has introduced a bill requiring congressional approval before such closures.
stories.w: The archive sits next door to Millbrae and is a key resource for Peninsula families tracing immigration and family records, fewer than 4% of which are digitized.

stories.t: Justice Department sues California to set aside 20,000 mailed ballots
stories.s: The U.S. Justice Department sued California and Los Angeles County election officials on Thursday, asking a federal court to set aside, and block the counting of, mail ballots sent to more than 20,000 voters it says are likely noncitizens. Secretary of State Shirley Weber said the state has not seen data backing the claim and will not disenfranchise voters on that basis, and legal experts note similar federal suits have failed. Ballots are already out statewide ahead of the Nov. 3 election.
stories.w: Nothing has changed yet for San Mateo County voters, but the case could affect how ballots are handled statewide in the final weeks before Election Day.

stories.t: Construction begins on 501 apartments at Redwood City’s Elco Yards
stories.s: High Street Residential has started building two apartment buildings with 501 units at Elco Yards in Redwood City, with completion expected in 2029. The El Camino Real building will include about 5,300 square feet of ground-floor retail. The groundbreaking follows a 2025 City Council vote that reduced the number of units reserved for lower-income households, a change the developer said it needed to make the project financially feasible.
stories.w: New homes on the El Camino corridor add supply in a county with steep rents, though fewer will be priced for low-income households than first planned.

stories.t: California gas averages $6.26 as the Iran war drives prices up nationwide
stories.s: California drivers are paying an average of $6.26 a gallon, far above the $4.33 national average, after Iranian attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz sent oil prices soaring. U.S. prices have risen $1.35 a gallon since the war began, and the national average hit a record in September. Democrats are now running ads blaming Republicans for the spike, while Republicans point to California’s gas tax and climate rules.
stories.w: Higher pump prices hit Peninsula commuters directly and are becoming a central issue in California’s competitive House races.

stories.t: Today in sports: Quakes chase a playoff spot, 49ers prep for Monday night
stories.s: The Warriors hosted Portland at Chase Center on Friday night in a preseason game, playing without Kristaps Porzingis, Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody; their regular season opens Wednesday at the Lakers. The Earthquakes host league-leading Nashville SC tonight at 7:30 at PayPal Park, and the 5-0 49ers host Washington on Monday Night Football at 5:15 p.m. The Golden State Valkyries also open the WNBA Finals against the Atlanta Dream today.

stories.t: Earthquakes can clinch first playoff berth since 2023 against Nashville
stories.s: San Jose (13-8-8) is fourth in the Western Conference and unbeaten in eight league matches, and a win over Nashville SC tonight would clinch its first playoff trip since 2023. Nashville (20-3-6) is one win from wrapping up the Supporters’ Shield. The Quakes earned a 1-1 draw at Real Salt Lake on Wednesday on Jack Jasinski’s stoppage-time equalizer, with Angus Gunn making six saves.

stories.t: 49ers open practice window for Christian Kirk ahead of Washington
stories.s: The 49ers promoted defensive lineman Ogbo Okoronkwo to the active roster and opened the practice window for receiver Christian Kirk as they prepare for Monday’s home game against Washington. They also added linebacker Eugene Asante to the practice squad. San Francisco is 5-0 and in first place in the NFC West after last Sunday’s 32-29 win at Seattle.

stories.t: Street Fighter brings the video game brawlers to theaters
stories.s: Paramount and Legendary’s Street Fighter, based on Capcom’s fighting games, opened Friday in theaters and IMAX after debuting in several overseas markets earlier in the week. Directed by Kitao Sakurai, the PG-13 film stars Noah Centineo, Andrew Koji, Callina Liang, Jason Momoa and David Dastmalchian, and carries a reported $82 million budget. Weekend estimates arrive Sunday.

stories.t: Gaza-raised, Bay Area-based rapper MC Abdul releases his debut album
stories.s: MC Abdul, an 18-year-old Palestinian rapper who grew up in Gaza and now lives in the Bay Area, released his nine-track debut album, Day by Day, Shway Shway, on Friday through San Francisco label EMPIRE. Producer Illmind built its Afrobeats-inspired beats. He performs today at Palestine Culture Day in Redwood City.

stories.t: Black Panther Party’s 60th anniversary celebrations wrap up in Oakland
stories.s: Events marking 60 years since the Black Panther Party’s founding continue this weekend, with workshops, a 25th-anniversary screening of A Huey P. Newton Story and an anniversary gala tonight featuring co-founder Bobby Seale. A free community day with live music follows Sunday at Bobby Hutton Park in West Oakland.

stories.t: Falcon 9 launches a classified Space Force payload from Vandenberg
stories.s: A SpaceX Falcon 9 lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base on the Central Coast at 5:01 p.m. Thursday carrying a classified payload for the U.S. Space Force on the USSF-481 mission. No details about the satellite’s purpose were released.

stories.t: CHP holds driver, not Tesla, responsible after sleeping motorist on Full Self-Driving hits patrol car
stories.s: The CHP says a driver using Tesla’s Full Self-Driving system told officers he was asleep when his car struck a patrol car on I-80 in Fairfield late Tuesday, seriously injuring two officers who have since been released from the hospital. The agency stressed that FSD is a driver-assistance system that requires constant supervision and is holding the driver responsible. Investigators will pull the car’s data and may ask the DMV to revoke his license.

stories.t: Ballots stolen from a Daly City post office; San Mateo County voters urged to check theirs
stories.s: An unknown number of San Mateo County vote-by-mail ballots were in mail stolen from a Daly City post office, and the county elections office is investigating with the US Postal Service after learning of the theft Wednesday. Voters who are worried can request a replacement ballot online by Oct. 27 or in person at any vote center, and can track their ballot through the state’s free Where’s My Ballot service.
stories.w: Any San Mateo County voter, including in Millbrae, can sign up for ballot tracking to confirm their ballot is mailed, received and counted.

stories.t: Southbound 101 closes in San Francisco this weekend as the Valkyries host the WNBA Finals
stories.s: Caltrans is closing southbound Highway 101 near Hospital Curve from 11 p.m. Friday to 6 a.m. Monday. The closure overlaps the Golden State Valkyries’ WNBA Finals home games against the Atlanta Dream at Chase Center, at 12:30 p.m. Saturday and 5 p.m. Monday, and Caltrain is urging fans to ride to Fourth and King, where Muni light rail is free with a game ticket.
stories.w: Drivers heading home to the Peninsula from San Francisco should expect detours and delays all weekend; Caltrain from Millbrae avoids the closure.

stories.t: BART will swap trains for buses between Daly City and 24th Street on Nov. 14–15
stories.s: BART will halt trains between 24th St. Mission and Daly City the weekend of Nov. 14–15 to install equipment for its new train control system, with SamTrans express buses and Muni shuttles filling the gap. The Green Line will be canceled, Red Line trains will turn back at 24th St. Mission, trains between Daly City and Millbrae will run every 15 minutes, and riders south of 24th St. should plan on delays of up to 30 minutes.
stories.w: Millbrae and SFO riders heading into San Francisco that weekend will have to switch to a bus at Daly City and should budget extra time.

stories.t: California’s next governor faces hard choices on Medi-Cal
stories.s: Medi-Cal covers about 13.6 million Californians, roughly 1 in 3, and now costs $222 billion a year, more than 40% of state spending, just as federal cuts of more than $900 billion over a decade begin. Republican Steve Hilton wants to narrow eligibility and end coverage for immigrants without legal status, while Democrat Xavier Becerra pledges to shield residents from federal cuts but hasn’t said how the state would pay. An enrollment freeze for undocumented adults and new monthly premiums take effect next year.
stories.w: About a third of Californians rely on Medi-Cal, so the governor’s race will shape coverage for many San Mateo County families.

stories.t: Teen gunman kills three children and a teacher at an Oregon elementary school
stories.s: A 16-year-old opened fire at an elementary school in Bend, Oregon, killing three children and a teacher. An armed community member then shot and killed the suspect.
stories.w: The attack in central Oregon is likely to renew questions about school safety plans in districts across the West Coast, including the Bay Area.

stories.t: Today in sports: Quakes host league-leading Nashville Saturday; 49ers get ready for Washington
stories.s: Fresh off Wednesday’s stoppage-time draw in Utah, the Earthquakes, unbeaten in eight and fourth in the West, host Nashville SC at PayPal Park on Saturday with a playoff berth in sight. The 5–0 49ers host Washington on Monday night without suspended linebacker Dre Greenlaw, the Warriors play their final preseason game before Wednesday’s opener at the Lakers, and the Bay Area’s Valkyries open the WNBA Finals at Chase Center on Saturday.

stories.t: New this weekend: “Street Fighter” in theaters, Chris Evans in Netflix’s “Sacrifice,” and a new Fontaines D.C. album
stories.s: In theaters, Paramount’s Street Fighter opens after $4 million in Thursday previews, alongside Whalefall, A24’s Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything and Sense and Sensibility. On streaming, Netflix has Sacrifice with Chris Evans and Anya Taylor-Joy, Prime Video has Stanley Tucci’s Mona Lisa heist Masterplan, Apple TV has the Everest drama Tenzing, and Tulsa King season 4 starts on Paramount+. New albums include Fontaines D.C.’s Dopamine Chamber, Babehoven’s I See Them, I See Me and The Avalanches’ No Bad Memories.

stories.t: Fontaines D.C. turn darker and more reflective on “Dopamine Chamber”
stories.s: The Dublin band’s fifth album, the follow-up to Romance, takes a darker, more reflective look at modern life and tops Radio Milwaukee’s picks for the week. Other standouts include June McDoom’s harmony-rich folk record Follow the Light, Babehoven’s I See Them, I See Me and new releases from Rachel Chinouriri, Eels and HAAI.

stories.t: Cargo Dragon docks at the space station with its last new solar arrays
stories.s: SpaceX’s CRS-35 Dragon, which launched Tuesday from Cape Canaveral, docked with the International Space Station at 7:27 a.m. Pacific on Thursday after a roughly 51-hour chase. It delivered more than 6,300 pounds of food, research gear and hardware, including the last of eight upgraded solar panels, and will stay about a month before returning to Earth.
